accepted.author: Ben Thompson
accepted.passage: The iPhone is the most successful product of all time. It is the most profitable product of all time. It is the most important product of all time.
accepted.feedback: Great parallel use of three sentences, good rhythm, decent punchy emotional impact

structure.template: [Subject] is the most [adjective1] [noun] of all time. It is the most [adjective2] [noun] of all time. It is the most [adjective3] [noun] of all time.
structure.technique: Tripled parallel with escalating significance (successful → profitable → important)

emotionalWeight.dryVersion: The iPhone has been commercially successful and culturally significant.
emotionalWeight.technique: Repetition creates gravity; parallel structure creates inevitability

usage.bestFor: Making bold claims feel earned through rhythmic weight

accepted.author: Paul Graham
accepted.passage: The way to get startup ideas is not to try to think of startup ideas. It's to look for problems, preferably problems you have yourself.
accepted.feedback: Great repetition, good ideas, good insight. Solid sentence. Use of contrast is great. Clear flow through thesis.

rhythm.beat: Negation then pivot, second sentence lands cleaner

structure.template: The way to [goal] is not to [obvious approach]. It's to [counterintuitive approach], preferably [specific version].
structure.technique: Contrarian pivot: 'not X, it's Y' with repetition of key term

emotionalWeight.dryVersion: Don't brainstorm startup ideas; instead identify problems you personally experience.
emotionalWeight.technique: Repetition of 'startup ideas' creates echo; contrast creates insight moment

accepted.author: Joan Didion
accepted.passage: We tell ourselves stories in order to live. The princess is caged in the consulate. The man with the candy will lead the children into the sea.
accepted.feedback: First part brilliant, strong ideas. Trimmed AI-contaminated portion.

rhythm.beat: Thesis punch, then two mysterious images

structure.template: [Universal statement about human nature]. [Mysterious image 1]. [Mysterious image 2].
structure.technique: Abstract thesis followed by concrete but unexplained images

emotionalWeight.dryVersion: Humans use narrative to make sense of existence.
emotionalWeight.technique: Juxtaposition of abstract claim with fairy-tale imagery creates unease

usage.bestFor: Creating atmosphere, inviting reader into mystery

accepted.author: George Orwell
accepted.passage: The great enemy of clear language is insincerity. When there is a gap between one's real and one's declared aims, one turns as it were instinctively to long words and exhausted idioms, like a cuttlefish spurting out ink.
accepted.feedback: Amazing passage. The metaphor at the end is very strong and original.

rhythm.beat: Punchy thesis (8 words), then long elaboration ending in vivid simile

structure.template: [Short declarative thesis]. [Elaboration with subordinate clauses], like [unexpected vivid metaphor].

emotionalWeight.dryVersion: Dishonest people use complex language to obscure their meaning.
emotionalWeight.technique: Animal metaphor (cuttlefish ink) makes abstract concept visceral and memorable

usage.bestFor: Making abstract concepts concrete through unexpected metaphor

accepted.author: Annie Dillard
accepted.passage: The sky snapped over the sun like a lens cover. The grass was white. The sun was going, and the world was wrong.
accepted.feedback: Love the imagery, would be flowery if overdone, needs to be used cautiously to not be flowery in tech essays.

structure.template: [Vivid simile of event]. [Stark short observation]. [Event] was [verb]ing, and [larger context] was [adjective].

emotionalWeight.dryVersion: The eclipse began and the light changed dramatically.
emotionalWeight.technique: Sensory details + short declarative creates visceral experience

accepted.caution: Use sparingly in tech context - becomes flowery if overdone

accepted.author: Ta-Nehisi Coates
accepted.passage: But race is the child of racism, not the father. And the process of naming 'the people' has never been a matter of genealogy and physiognomy so much as one of hierarchy.

structure.template: But [A] is the [relation] of [B], not the [inverse relation]. And [process] has never been a matter of [assumed cause] so much as one of [real cause].

emotionalWeight.dryVersion: Racism created the concept of race, not the other way around.
emotionalWeight.technique: Inversion of expected causality creates 'aha' moment

accepted.author: Virginia Woolf
accepted.passage: Lock up your libraries if you like; but there is no gate, no lock, no bolt that you can set upon the freedom of my mind.
accepted.feedback: Wonderful repetition 'no gate no lock no bolt that you can set upon' - great.

rhythm.beat: Concession (8 words) + triple negation building to climax

structure.template: [Concession to opponent]; but there is no [barrier1], no [barrier2], no [barrier3] that you can [action] upon [what you're defending].

emotionalWeight.dryVersion: Physical restrictions cannot limit intellectual freedom.
emotionalWeight.technique: Triple negation creates crescendo; 'freedom of my mind' lands as triumph

accepted.author: Christopher Hitchens
accepted.passage: The essence of the independent mind lies not in what it thinks, but in how it thinks.
accepted.feedback: Good sentence that introduces a strong contrarian idea.

structure.template: The essence of [subject] lies not in [surface quality], but in [deeper quality].

emotionalWeight.dryVersion: Independent thinking is about process, not conclusions.
emotionalWeight.technique: Balanced structure with pivot creates sense of revelation

usage.bestFor: Redefining concepts, shifting focus from surface to depth

accepted.author: Zadie Smith
accepted.passage: The very reason you write is so that you might not sleepwalk through your entire life.
accepted.feedback: Love this idea but be careful that it's not the structure but the idea itself that makes this work.

structure.template: The very reason you [activity] is so that you might not [vivid negative verb] through [scope].
structure.technique: Purpose statement with unexpected vivid verb

emotionalWeight.dryVersion: Writing helps you live more consciously.
emotionalWeight.technique: The verb 'sleepwalk' does all the work—concrete, physical, slightly haunting

accepted.caution: Idea carries it, not structure—the verb choice is everything

accepted.author: Steve Yegge
accepted.source: Execution in the Kingdom of Nouns
accepted.passage: Java is the Kingdom of Nouns. In the Kingdom of Nouns, you see, nouns are everywhere. Nouns own everything. Nouns run the show. Verbs are their slaves—humble, loyal, hardworking servants who must be attached to a noun at all times or face certain death.
accepted.feedback: Amazing. Amazing use of metaphor to teach something. Amazing emotional weight to a dry idea. Amazing repetition.

rhythm.beat: Four punchy setup sentences, then one elaborate payoff

structure.template: [Technical thing] is the [Metaphorical World]. In the [Metaphorical World], [metaphor elements] are everywhere. [Elements] own everything. [Elements] run the show. [Counter-elements] are their slaves—[elaboration].
structure.technique: Extended metaphor with worldbuilding + repetition + dramatic escalation

emotionalWeight.dryVersion: Java's object-oriented design requires wrapping all functionality in classes.
emotionalWeight.technique: Political/feudal metaphor makes technical design feel oppressive and absurd

accepted.author: Paul Graham
accepted.passage: When I finished grad school in computer science I went to art school to study painting. A lot of people seemed surprised that someone interested in computers would also be interested in painting. They seemed to think that hacking and painting were very different kinds of work—that hacking was cold, precise, and methodical, and that painting was the frenzied expression of some primal urge. Both of these images are wrong.
accepted.feedback: Great way to introduce a thesis or idea through a small story.

rhythm.beat: Personal fact → others' reaction → their assumption (detailed) → terse rebuttal

structure.template: [Personal anecdote about unexpected combination]. [Others' surprised reaction]. They seemed to think [assumption A] and [assumption B]. [Terse rebuttal].
structure.technique: Personal story → common assumption → short devastating pivot

emotionalWeight.dryVersion: Programming and art have more in common than people think.
emotionalWeight.technique: Building up the conventional wisdom at length, then knocking it down in 7 words

accepted.author: Ben Thompson
accepted.passage: The value chain for any given consumer market is divided into three parts: suppliers, distributors, and consumers. The best way to make outsize profits in any of these markets is to either gain a horizontal monopoly in one of the three parts or to integrate two of the parts such that you have a competitive advantage in delivering a vertical solution.
accepted.feedback: Clear solid prose, likely in middle parts of the essay.

structure.template: [Domain] is divided into [N] parts: [list]. The best way to [goal] is to either [strategy A] or [strategy B].

emotionalWeight.dryVersion: Markets have suppliers, distributors, and consumers. Profits come from monopoly or vertical integration.
emotionalWeight.technique: Minimal—this is explanatory prose. Clarity is the goal, not emotion.

accepted.author: Venkatesh Rao
accepted.passage: The Gervais Principle is this: Sociopaths, in their own best interests, knowingly promote over-performing losers into middle-management, groom under-performing losers into sociopaths, and game the system to retain the most capable losers by manipulating their motivation.
accepted.feedback: Brilliant use of wordplay on the idea of 'losers'. Will require advanced thought to bring this idea to life, good repetition.

rhythm.beat: Naming + colon + three parallel actions with 'losers' repeated

structure.template: The [Framework Name] is this: [Agent], in their own best interests, [action1 with repeated term], [action2 with repeated term], and [action3 with repeated term].
structure.technique: Framework naming + tripled parallel structure with word repetition

emotionalWeight.dryVersion: Organizations have three tiers with different incentives and mobility patterns.
emotionalWeight.technique: Redefining 'loser' across different contexts creates cognitive dissonance and insight

accepted.caution: Requires advanced execution—the redefinition must be earned

accepted.author: Maciej Cegłowski
accepted.source: The Internet With A Human Face
accepted.passage: We have a word for this kind of organism. We call it a parasite. A parasite that spies on you, learns your habits, and uses that information to manipulate your behavior. And we've invited this parasite into our homes, our bedrooms, our pockets.
accepted.feedback: Wonderful sentence. The varied rhythm paired with an emotional idea, that everyone carries their phone and it is not a parasite.

rhythm.beat: Setup → naming → elaboration → universal application (escalating intimacy: homes → bedrooms → pockets)

structure.template: We have a word for [thing]. We call it a [loaded metaphor]. A [metaphor] that [action1], [action2], and [action3]. And we've invited this [metaphor] into [place1], [place2], [place3].

emotionalWeight.dryVersion: Tech companies collect personal data from devices we keep with us constantly.
emotionalWeight.technique: Parasitic metaphor + escalating intimacy (homes→bedrooms→pockets) creates visceral unease

usage.bestFor: Making abstract harms feel personal and invasive

accepted.author: Andy Matuschak
accepted.passage: Books don't work for the same reason that lectures don't work: our minds are not designed to absorb information passively. We learn by doing, by struggling, by failing, by connecting new ideas to old ones. A book asks nothing of you. It just sits there, waiting.
accepted.feedback: Love the idea and the repetition and the contrarian concept. Love the way that he brings a book to life 'it just sits there, waiting' - wonderful.

rhythm.beat: Argument → evidence (quadrupled 'by') → personification setup → haunting close

structure.template: [Medium A] doesn't work for the same reason [Medium B] doesn't work: [reason]. We [learn/achieve] by [method1], by [method2], by [method3], by [method4]. [Medium A] asks nothing of you. It just [anthropomorphic action].
structure.technique: Parallel comparison → quadrupled 'by' repetition → personification punch

emotionalWeight.dryVersion: Passive learning is ineffective; active engagement is required.
emotionalWeight.technique: Personifying the book ('It just sits there, waiting') creates eerie accusation

usage.bestFor: Contrarian claims, making inanimate things feel alive and implicated

rejected.author: Kevin Kelly
rejected.reason: Lots of buzz words, not a lot of substance

rejected.author: James Baldwin
rejected.passage: I had discovered the weight of white people in the world. I could not have known what this was but I knew that whatever was going on in my life, I knew that whatever was happening to me had something to do with what they wanted to do.
rejected.reason: Strong sentence but could only masterfully work because of Baldwin's great style - style-dependent, not transferable

rejected.author: Joel Spolsky
rejected.passage: All non-trivial abstractions, to some degree, are leaky. Abstractions fail. Sometimes a little, sometimes a lot. There's leakage. Things go wrong. It happens all over the place when you have abstractions.
rejected.reason: Seems too common of standard AI prose these days

rejected.author: Bret Victor
rejected.passage: Here's something I've come to believe: Every creator should have an immediate connection to what they're creating. That's my principle. And this is not about tools. This is about a way of thinking. A way of seeing. A way of creating.
rejected.reason: Staccato 'A way of X. A way of Y. A way of Z.' pattern reads too AI

rejected.author: Nadia Eghbal
rejected.passage: Open source developers are not volunteers in the traditional sense. They are not building houses for the poor or serving food at a soup kitchen. They are more like street performers, or buskers: artists who perform in public, for the love of their craft, and who are frequently ignored by the people who benefit from their work.
rejected.reason: Ok but not as strong as others

rejected.author: Patrick McKenzie
rejected.passage: Negotiation is not a battle. It is not a war. It is a conversation where you attempt to understand what the other side values, communicate what you value, and find a way to make both sides better off than they were before the conversation started.

rejected.author: Eugene Wei
rejected.passage: What all of social media has in common is that it involves humans competing for status. All social networks have this in common, and it's a feature, not a bug. Humans are status-seeking monkeys. We always have been.
rejected.reason: Don't like cliches like 'it's a feature, not a bug'

avoidRules.name: buzzword-soup
avoidRules.description: Passages filled with trendy terms but lacking substance
avoidRules.example: Synergizing our core competencies to leverage disruptive innovation
avoidRules.detection: High ratio of abstract nouns to concrete claims

avoidRules.name: tech-cliche
examples: it's a feature, not a bug

avoidRules.name: ai-staccato-pattern
avoidRules.description: Series of very short punchy sentences—now associated with AI prose
avoidRules.example: Things break. Systems fail. Abstractions leak. It happens.

avoidRules.name: ai-tripled-fragment
avoidRules.description: 'A way of X. A way of Y. A way of Z.' parallel fragments
avoidRules.example: This is about a way of thinking. A way of seeing. A way of creating.

avoidRules.name: author-voice-dependent
avoidRules.description: Prose that only works because of a specific author's established voice
avoidRules.example: Baldwin's rhythms require his full context
avoidRules.detection: Relies on cumulative authorial ethos, not transferable pattern

avoidRules.name: em-dash-kitschy
avoidRules.description: Overuse of em-dashes for dramatic pause, especially in short sentences
avoidRules.detection: Em-dash used for effect rather than parenthetical

avoidRules.name: flowery-overdone
avoidRules.description: Too much imagery/poetic language for tech context
avoidRules.example: The code danced across the screen like autumn leaves
avoidRules.detection: Metaphor density inappropriate for technical subject

emulateRules.name: original-metaphor-punch
emulateRules.description: End elaboration with unexpected, vivid metaphor
emulateRules.example: like a cuttlefish spurting out ink
emulateRules.technique: Save concrete image for end of abstract discussion

emulateRules.name: tripled-negation
emulateRules.description: Three parallel negatives building to defiant claim
emulateRules.example: no gate, no lock, no bolt that you can set upon

emulateRules.name: personal-story-pivot
emulateRules.description: Personal anecdote → others' assumption → terse rebuttal
emulateRules.example: Paul Graham's art school story ending with 'Both of these images are wrong.'
emulateRules.technique: Build up conventional wisdom at length, demolish in few words

emulateRules.name: dry-concept-worldbuilding
emulateRules.description: Turn technical concept into political/social metaphor with characters
emulateRules.example: Yegge's Kingdom of Nouns where verbs are slaves

emulateRules.name: not-X-but-Y
emulateRules.description: Antithetical structure pivoting from surface to depth
emulateRules.example: lies not in what it thinks, but in how it thinks

emulateRules.name: personification-punch
emulateRules.description: Give inanimate thing human behavior for closing impact
emulateRules.technique: Short sentence, anthropomorphic verb, slight menace

emulateRules.name: wordplay-redefinition
emulateRules.description: Use same word with shifting meaning across contexts
emulateRules.example: Rao's 'losers' meaning different things in different positions

emulateRules.name: escalating-intimacy
emulateRules.description: List that moves from public to private spaces
emulateRules.technique: Each item more personal than the last

emulateRules.name: quadrupled-by
emulateRules.example: by doing, by struggling, by failing, by connecting

emulateRules.name: uniform-parallel-escalation
emulateRules.description: Same sentence structure repeated with escalating significance
emulateRules.example: most successful... most profitable... most important
emulateRules.technique: Identical rhythm, increasing weight of adjective
